text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.1% today, extending a week-long decline from its peak of $414.65 on November 13th. The drop comes as crude oil prices have retreated to $89.62 per barrel (down from levels above $92 earlier in the week), which directly pressures refiner profitability—these companies make money on the spread between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for, so lower oil prices compress those margins. Additionally, refineries are running at 95.2% capacity with high inventory levels (gasoline stocks at 210.7 million barrels), suggesting the market isn't tight enough to support strong margins right now.

The broader context includes geopolitical risk that briefly supported oil prices earlier in the week—Iran's escalating threats and a third U.S. carrier in the Middle East had the potential to disrupt supply. As those headlines faded and no actual disruption materialized, the supporting effect on crude prices unwound, leaving refiners facing the fundamental reality of soft demand signals (holiday shipping caution, heating oil demand concerns) and ample supply.
